'''Christopher Alexander Hunter''', [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]] (born 19 February 1965) is a British [[chemist]] and academic. Since 2014, he has been [[Herchel Smith]] Professor of [[Organic Chemistry]] in the [[Department of Chemistry, University of Cambridge|Department of Chemistry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="Who's Who 2014">{{cite web|title=HUNTER, Prof. Christopher Alexander|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U247063|website=Who's Who 2014|publisher=A & C Black|accessdate=2015-02-20|date=November 2014}}</ref><ref name="Department of Chemistry - Herchel Smith Professor of Organic Chemistry">{{cite web|title=Herchel Smith Professor of Organic Chemistry|url=http://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/news/herchel-smith-professor-organic-chemistry|website=Department of Chemistry|publisher=University of Cambridge|accessdate=2015-02-20|date=2 September 2013}}</ref> His research is currently focused on [[molecular recognition]].<ref name="RSC - Physical Organic Chemistry Award Winner 2011">{{cite web|title=Physical Organic Chemistry Award Winner 2011|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/PhysicalOrganicChemistryAward/2011winner.asp|website=Awards|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|accessdate=2015-02-20}}</ref><ref name="bio - Royal Society" /> He was previously a lecturer at the [[University of Otago]] and a lecturer then professor at the [[University of Sheffield]].

==Early life and education==
Hunter was born on 19 February 1965 in [[Dunedin]], New Zealand. He is the son of John Alexander Hunter and his wife Alice Mary Hunter.<ref name="Who's Who 2014" /> He and his family moved to [[Northern Ireland]] in 1969.<ref name="bio - Department of Chemistry">{{cite web|title=Professor Chris Hunter FRS|url=http://www.ch.cam.ac.uk/person/ch664|website=Department of Chemistry|publisher=University of Cambridge|accessdate=2015-02-20}}</ref><ref name="bio - Royal Society" /> He was educated at Portstewart Primary School and the [[Coleraine Academical Institution]], an all-boys [[grammar school]] in [[Coleraine]], County Londonderry.<ref name="bio - Department of Chemistry" /> He studied [[Natural Sciences (Cambridge)|Natural Sciences]] and then [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Cambridge]].<ref name="bio - Emmanuel College, Cambridge" /> He graduated with a Bachelor of Arts (BA) degree in 1986, this was later promoted to [[Master of Arts (Oxbridge and Dublin)|Master of Arts]] (MA Cantab) as per tradition, and with a Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degree in 1989.<ref name="Department of Chemistry - Herchel Smith Professor of Organic Chemistry" />

==Career and research==
Hunter returned to [[New Zealand]] to begin his academic career. He was a lecturer in [[bioorganic chemistry]] at the [[University of Otago]] from 1989 to 1991.<ref name="Who's Who 2014" /><ref name="bio - Emmanuel College, Cambridge" /> He then returned to the United Kingdom and joined the [[University of Sheffield]].<ref name="bio - Royal Society" /> He was a lecturer from 1991 to 1994 and [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]] from 1994 to 1997.<ref name="Who's Who 2014" /> He was promoted to professor of chemistry in 1997.<ref name="Department of Chemistry - Herchel Smith Professor of Organic Chemistry" /> He held a [[Lister Institute]] Research Fellowship from 1994 to 1999, and an [[Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council]] Senior Research Fellowship from 2005 to 2010.<ref name="bio - Department of Chemistry" />

In September 2013, he was selected as the next [[Herchel Smith]] Professor of [[Organic Chemistry]]. He joined the [[University of Cambridge]] in early 2014 to take up the appointment.<ref name="Department of Chemistry - Herchel Smith Professor of Organic Chemistry" /> There, he is a member of the Synthetic Chemistry Research Interest Group.<ref name="bio - Department of Chemistry" /> He is also a [[Fellow]] of [[Emmanuel College, Cambridge]].<ref name="bio - Emmanuel College, Cambridge">{{cite web|title=Professor Christopher Hunter|url=http://www.emma.cam.ac.uk/contact/fellows/?id=347|website=Fellows|publisher=Emmanuel College, Cambridge|accessdate=2015-02-20}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In 2008, Hunter married Rosaleen Theresa McHugh. Together they have three children; two sons and one daughter.<ref name="Who's Who 2014" />

==Awards and honours==
In 1992, Hunter was jointly awarded the [[Meldola Medal and Prize]] by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref name="Who's Who 2014" /> It is awarded to a British chemist who was under 32 years of age for promising original investigations in chemistry. In 1999, he was jointly awarded the [[Corday-Morgan Prizes|Corday–Morgan Medal and Prize]] by the Royal Society of Chemistry.<ref name="Who's Who 2014" /> It is awarded for 'the most meritorious contributions to chemistry'.<ref>{{cite web|title=Corday-Morgan Prizes|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/CordayMorganPrizes/|website=Awards|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|accessdate=2015-02-20}}</ref> In 2008, he was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS), the premier [[learned society]] and [[national academy]] for science in the United Kingdom.<ref name="bio - Royal Society">{{cite web|title=Professor Chris Hunter FRS|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/chris-hunter/|website=People|publisher=Royal Society|accessdate=2015-02-20}}</ref>
